newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds slip, spreads widen a fraction.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds slip, spreads widen a fraction.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backeds dipped into negative territory in late-afternoon trade, ending three consecutive sessions of above-par levels.
Pass-through yield spreads to comparable Treasuries were a hair wider, but narrowed about two basis points from yesterday's close, mortgage experts said.
"Yield spreads recouped some of their widening from last night. Now they are just a (fraction) on the wider side," said one pass-through trader.
Light buying bolstered mortgage prices earlier in the session, but pass-throughs quickly succumbed to selling in directional trade with Treasuries, another trader said.
No major bid lists were spotted, he said.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were off 7/32 at 100-17/32 bid, yielding 105 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was off 5/32 at 100-12/32 bid, and Freddie Mac issues fell back 6/32 at 100-17/32 bid.
The five-year Treasury note was down 4/32 to yield 6.31 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was off 7/32 to yield 6.43 percent.

Debt market players got some relief after the release of soft U.S. consumer price data, which enhanced the prospects for Federal Reserve policymakers to leave short-term interest rates unchanged at their July 1-2 meeting.

The U.S. Labor Department reported a 0.1-percent rise in consumer prices for May, following a 0.2 percent increase in April. Wall Street experts had expected a 0.2-percent gain, a Reuters poll showed.
